chapters.chapter: Getting started: setup, formats and help

capabilities.capability: Published system, GPU and hardware requirements plus a list of every import and export format and codec the app reads or writes.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios check a workstation or render node against the list before a job, and confirm a client's codec is readable before footage arrives.

match.note: engine.doctor checks the machine (core, audio, tools) and prints the exact fix for each gap; engine.info reports the renderers and tool versions found. Doodleberry has no general codec matrix because it reads few footage formats.

capabilities.capability: Preferences for application-wide defaults: auto-save, default interpolation, still-sequence frame rate, import interpretation rules, cache locations.
capabilities.pro_use: A facility sets house defaults once so every artist's comps start the same way.

match.note: House defaults live in versioned data: dbe/profiles.json (encoding profiles, per-style QA thresholds) and schema defaults. There is no per-user preferences store; it is not needed for agents.

capabilities.capability: Customisable keyboard shortcuts with a visual keyboard map.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators remap keys to speed up repetitive keyframing and timeline work.

match.note: Doodleberry is driven by commands from agents and people (CLI, HTTP, MCP, Studio); there is no keyboard-heavy editing surface whose shortcuts would need mapping.

capabilities.capability: A built-in AI assistant that answers how-to questions about the app and can carry out some actions in the project.
capabilities.pro_use: Newer artists ask it how to do a task instead of searching the manual; experienced users use it for repetitive setup.

match.note: Agent-native by design: engine.commands exposes every command with its input schema as an agent tool (MCP), so an agent can both explain and do. A chat beside the storyboard is WP-21.

capabilities.capability: Knowledge base of known issues, fixed issues and FAQs per release.
capabilities.pro_use: Teams check known issues before upgrading mid-production.

match.note: In-house tool with its history in git and the docs (docs/build-plan.md, feature map); docs.check keeps the docs and command registry in agreement, but a public issue knowledge base has no role here.

capabilities.capability: Dockable, saveable workspaces made of panels (project, composition viewer, timeline, effect controls, properties) arranged per task.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists keep separate layouts for animation, compositing, review and text work and switch between them per stage.

match.note: Studio has fixed pages per task (/timeline, /board, /plan, Rig Canvas, /doodle, /actout) built on timeline.get and the player page from film.preview; user-arranged panels and a director's desk combining storyboard, animatic and chat are WP-21.

capabilities.capability: A context-sensitive Properties panel showing the most-used controls of whatever layer is selected, editable in place.
capabilities.pro_use: Motion designers tweak position, scale, text and shape settings without opening the layer's full property tree.

match.note: timeline.edit edits clip layers from the Studio timeline and film.write writes any source file with validation; an in-place property inspector for every shot, cast and overlay field is not built (Studio timeline 2, WP-19).

capabilities.capability: The core workflow: create a project, build compositions from footage and layers, animate, add effects, preview, then render.
capabilities.pro_use: Every job follows this spine, which teams map onto their own stages and checklists.

match.note: Doodleberry's spine is data-first: film.create, edit brief/facts/script/shots with film.write, preview with film.preview, then film.render (which also mixes and runs QA).

capabilities.capability: A project file that references (not copies) footage and organises items into folders, with relinking of missing or replaced files.
capabilities.pro_use: Large jobs keep hundreds of assets in a tidy folder structure and swap a placeholder for final art in one step.

match.note: A film is a folder of text files referencing cast puppets and sets by path; replacing a puppet file updates every shot that uses it. film.get returns the whole set.

capabilities.capability: Composition settings: frame size, pixel aspect ratio, frame rate, duration, background colour, start timecode.
capabilities.pro_use: Deliverable specs (9:16 social, 16:9 broadcast, 24/25/30 fps) are fixed per composition at the start of a job.

match.note: Size and fps are film fields validated on write; aspects re-stage one film natively for 16:9 and 1:1. Pixel aspect and timecode are not modelled (square pixels only).

capabilities.capability: Nesting and pre-composing: grouping layers into a sub-composition that can be reused, transformed and effected as one layer.
capabilities.pro_use: Character rigs, lower thirds and repeated graphics are built once as precomps and dropped into many shots.

match.note: Puppets and kit elements are reusable units and film.cuts can insert segments from other films' renders, but a shot cannot contain another shot or group arbitrary layers; nested scene graphs belong with the per-shot compositor (WP-36).

capabilities.capability: Composition and layer markers holding comments, chapter points, cue points and durations.
capabilities.pro_use: Editors and animators mark beats, sync points and client notes on the timeline.

match.note: Spoken lines are named time anchors ('hi.start+0.2') that any time field can reference, cues mark sound events and film.beats reports the beat grid; frame notes are review.add (see Collaboration).

capabilities.capability: Composition Profiler showing how much render time each layer, effect and mask costs.
capabilities.pro_use: Compositors find the one expensive effect that is slowing previews and renders.

match.note: No per-element cost breakdown. WP-20 brings a measured cost and time estimate before rendering; per-element profiling should join it.

capabilities.capability: Pre-rendering a heavy nested composition and swapping the render in as a proxy.
capabilities.pro_use: Finished background passes are baked once so the rest of the comp previews quickly.

match.note: film.render re-renders only shots whose content hash changed and dedupes identical frames; a static-layer cache for unchanging set layers is WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Project and composition templates to start new jobs from a standard structure.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios start every episode of a series from the same template project with naming and render settings in place.

match.note: film.from_template builds a storyboard from a format template (myth vs data, explainer, dialogue) and a brief; film.create makes an empty film.

capabilities.capability: Auto-save and incremental versions of the project file.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists recover from crashes and roll back to an earlier version of a shot.

match.note: Films are text under version control, so every change is a diffable commit and any old version re-renders exactly (frames are pure functions of time).

capabilities.capability: Scene Edit Detection: finding the cuts inside an imported edited video and splitting it into layers.
capabilities.pro_use: Used when an offline edit or a reference cut arrives as one flat movie.

match.note: Doodleberry builds pictures from shot data, so shot boundaries are always known; it does not ingest flattened edits.

capabilities.capability: Importing layered Photoshop and Illustrator files as compositions, keeping each layer separate and editable.
capabilities.pro_use: Illustrators design characters and backgrounds in layered files that animators bring in with layers intact.

match.note: puppet.import reads layered SVG, PSD and ORA and builds a rig from layer names (parts, swaps, pivot markers); Krita .kra and Illustrator .ai import are WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Importing SVG files directly as editable vector shape layers (added in the 26.0 release).
capabilities.pro_use: Vector assets from design tools come in without a detour through Illustrator.

match.note: Layered SVG is a native input of puppet.import (as puppet parts, not free-floating shape layers in a shot).

capabilities.capability: Importing video and audio footage and interpreting it: frame rate, field order, pixel aspect, looping, start timecode.
capabilities.pro_use: Live-action plates, stock clips and reference video are conformed to the composition's settings before compositing.

match.note: Shots have no footage layer; video is only read as performance input (actout.clip). A video or plate layer belongs with the compositor (WP-36).

capabilities.capability: Interpreting alpha as straight or premultiplied to avoid fringes on semi-transparent edges.
capabilities.pro_use: Compositors fix halos on rendered elements from other packages.

match.note: Internally Synfig and Grease Pencil renders are composited with alpha over the set by ffmpeg; user-supplied footage with alpha needs WP-36 (and alpha outputs WP-23).

capabilities.capability: Importing still images and numbered image sequences (PNG, TIFF, EXR) as footage.
capabilities.pro_use: Painted backgrounds, hand-drawn frame sequences and CG passes arrive as stills or sequences.

match.note: Photos and scans become raster-part puppets (puppet.from_ink, doodle.snap); a sequence of drawings with exposures is the drawn-level part type in WP-35. Painted background plates as set layers would sit in WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Recorded voice-over and music import, placed on the timeline and synced to picture.
capabilities.pro_use: Productions bring in recorded dialogue and licensed music and cut the picture to them.

match.note: Narration slots and word alignment exist (script.slots, voice.build aligns words); fitting recorded human takes into slots with phone-level alignment is WP-13.

capabilities.capability: Importing 3D models (glTF, GLB, OBJ and, since 25.2, FBX) into a composition.
capabilities.pro_use: Motion designers drop product models or props into 2D designs and light them in place.

match.note: puppet.from_blend flattens a Blender cut-out rig into a 2D puppet; GLB models play in the three.js 3D pages (tools/three/run3d.mjs, e.g. films/screwworm-3d) but not through a command. 3D sets and models in films are WP-42.

capabilities.capability: HDR footage import and export with colour metadata (HLG and PQ, CICP tags; extended in 25.4).
capabilities.pro_use: HDR deliverables for streaming and broadcast keep correct colour tags end to end.

match.note: SDR only today; an HDR master is in WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Importing Premiere Pro sequences and After Effects projects into a project.
capabilities.pro_use: Editors send a cut to motion graphics, who rebuild it as compositions.

match.note: film.cuts writes OTIO per cut for editors; reading timelines back in (FCPXML, EDL, round trips through melt) is WP-22.

capabilities.capability: Many layer types: footage, solids, text, shapes, nulls, adjustment layers, cameras and lights, all stacked in one timeline.
capabilities.pro_use: Everything in a motion graphics shot is a layer, so artists build scenes by stacking and ordering them.

match.note: A shot has a fixed stack: set, underlays, cast, overlays (kit elements, signs, text), bubbles, then film-level captions, plus camera keys. No free solids, nulls or adjustment layers; those come with the compositor (WP-36).

capabilities.capability: Layer in and out points, trimming, sliding and splitting layers in time.
capabilities.pro_use: Editors retime when a graphic appears and cut a layer to reuse half of it.

match.note: Clip layers move and resize with timeline.edit; shot, overlay and cue times are start/end fields (line-relative allowed). Dragging lines and shots in Studio is WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Parenting layers to each other and to null objects so children inherit transforms.
capabilities.pro_use: Rigs and grouped graphics are driven from one controller null.

match.note: Hierarchy exists inside puppets and for props passing from hand to hand; arbitrary parenting between unrelated shot elements does not.

capabilities.capability: Transform properties on every layer: anchor point, position, scale, rotation, opacity, each keyframable.
capabilities.pro_use: The basic vocabulary of motion graphics: moves, pops, spins and fades.

match.note: Characters have place keys (x, y, scale, flip) and per-part angles via clips; kit elements have position, size and start/end with built-in fades. Whole-element rotation and opacity keys are missing; general layer transforms should land with WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Blending modes (multiply, screen, add, overlay, colour dodge and others) per layer.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for light effects, shadows, textures laid over art and colour treatments.

match.note: No user-facing blend modes; the node compositor (WP-36) lists them.

capabilities.capability: Layer styles such as drop shadow, inner glow, bevel and stroke, editable like Photoshop styles.
capabilities.pro_use: Quick finishing on text and logos.

match.note: Only ground shadows and toon cel shading/rims exist; the AI-look lint (WP-04) deliberately flags drop shadows and glows, so styles would be opt-in within WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Layer and composition markers that carry comments, durations and cue information.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators note client feedback and sync points directly on layers.

match.note: review.add pins a note to a frame; review.list shows notes with status. Sync points are line-relative times and cues (see Projects).

capabilities.capability: 3D layers: any 2D layer can move and rotate in X, Y and Z and be seen through a camera.
capabilities.pro_use: Motion designers build 2.5D parallax scenes from flat artwork.

match.note: No 2.5D layers in shot films; true 2D multiplane depth (layers on planes, parallax) is WP-36. Code-built three.js pages exist for full 3D (see 3D chapter).

capabilities.capability: Camera moves on a 2D frame: pan, zoom, push-in, follow a subject, handheld shake.
capabilities.pro_use: Directors add life and emphasis without redrawing art.

match.note: Camera keys are baked into every renderer; camera_auto frames the speaker, eases between shots, punches in on emphasis and adds seeded handheld; float adds slow drift.

capabilities.capability: 3D cameras (one-node and two-node) with focal length, point of interest, orbit and depth of field.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for dimensional fly-throughs and focus pulls across layered art.

match.note: Camera is 2D (centre and zoom). Depth of field is available only as blur filters in hand-coded scene.js films (engine/draw.js); a multiplane camera with depth of field is WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Lights (point, spot, parallel, ambient, environment) that shade 3D layers and cast shadows.
capabilities.pro_use: Lighting gives flat art depth and mood and unifies elements from different sources.

match.note: style.toon gives a fixed-direction cel shadow and rim on vector parts, which is the 2D answer; real lights on layers or models come with the 3D layer (WP-42).

capabilities.capability: Continuous rasterisation of vector layers so they stay sharp at any scale.
capabilities.pro_use: Logos and shapes can be pushed in close without softening.

match.note: Vector puppets, sets and kit elements are drawn as SVG every frame, so they are resolution-independent (4K for free); raster parts are the exception.

capabilities.capability: Quick Offset (25.4): staggering the timing of several selected layers or keyframes in one gesture.
capabilities.pro_use: Cascading reveals of lists, letters or icons in seconds.

match.note: Staggers exist inside kit elements (title per_word, draw stagger) and acting; a general stagger edit on many selected items in the timeline belongs with timeline 2 (WP-19).

capabilities.capability: Keyframes on any property, with setting, selecting, copying, pasting and moving keys across layers.
capabilities.pro_use: The base of all hand animation and motion graphics work.

ref: shots.json keys (place, look, view, poses, ik, camera)
match.note: Keys are [time, value] pairs in film and puppet data, line-relative where useful; the Rig Canvas records keyed poses into clips. Not every field is keyable (e.g. element opacity).

capabilities.capability: Temporal interpolation choices per key: linear, Bezier, auto and continuous Bezier, and hold.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators control whether a move snaps, glides or cushions into a pose.

match.note: Clips ease between keys with a smooth curve, views and swaps hold, and the scene.js library (engine/timeline.js) offers named eases (cubic, expo, back). shots.json keys have no per-key interpolation choice; that comes with the curve editor (WP-19).

capabilities.capability: Graph Editor: value and speed graphs with tangent handles for shaping motion.
capabilities.pro_use: Senior animators polish timing and spacing on curves rather than by moving keys.

match.note: No curve editor; WP-19 lists a graph editor for keys.

capabilities.capability: Keyframe assistants: Easy Ease in/out, exponential scale, sequence layers, time-reverse keys.
capabilities.pro_use: One-click cushioning and quick sequencing of many layers.

match.note: Ease is the default, the principles filter adds anticipation and overshoot, and acting.plan sequences gestures from the voice; key-level assistants on a selection are WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Spatial interpolation and editable motion paths in the viewer, with auto-orient along the path.
capabilities.pro_use: Moves follow designed arcs; a plane or arrow turns to face where it is going.

match.note: Travel is straight or ballistic (props, with motion arcs from fx.arcs); follow-path constraints and walking along a path are WP-11.

capabilities.capability: Roving keyframes that redistribute timing so speed stays even along a multi-key path.
capabilities.pro_use: Smooth camera and object moves through several positions.

match.note: Not available; it is a key-editing feature for the curve editor work in WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Puppet tools: pins placed on flat artwork deform it as a mesh (position, starch, bend and advanced pins).
capabilities.pro_use: Flat illustrations get organic, rubbery motion without a full rig.

match.note: Doodleberry's puppets deform by skinned meshes, bendy limbs and N-bone chains with springs: a rig rather than pins, renderers other than SVG pending (WP-14).

capabilities.capability: Animating shape and mask paths by keying the path itself, morphing one outline into another.
capabilities.pro_use: Logo morphs, liquid transitions and shape-changing icons.

match.note: Shapes change by swap (drawing substitution), not by path morph; morphs between views are planned in WP-43, and general path morphing for graphics should join it.

capabilities.capability: Motion Sketch: recording a mouse drag in real time as position keyframes.
capabilities.pro_use: Quick organic paths for flies, sparks or a hand-held feel.

match.note: The Rig Canvas records drags into poses and clips that puppet.save stores; actout.clip turns a filmed performance into a clip.

capabilities.capability: Wiggler and Smoother assistants: adding seeded random variation to keys, or thinning noisy keys.
capabilities.pro_use: Organic jitter on flickers and handheld moves; cleaning tracked or recorded data.

match.note: Variation comes from seeded noise (camera handheld, idle, boil); actout.clip reduces recorded keys against the played curve.

capabilities.capability: Time remapping, time stretch, freeze frames and reverse playback of layers.
capabilities.pro_use: Speed ramps, holds on a pose and slow-motion beats.

match.note: Clip layers have a speed field and the sound-off cut warps film time through timewarp knots (film.soundoff); arbitrary per-shot ramps, freezes and reverse are not exposed. Editing them in the timeline fits WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Frame blending and pixel-motion interpolation when footage is retimed.
capabilities.pro_use: Smooth slow motion from footage shot at normal speed.

match.note: Picture is re-rendered at the warped time (every frame is a pure function of time), so there are no source frames to blend.

capabilities.capability: Per-layer motion blur with shutter angle and phase.
capabilities.pro_use: Fast motion graphics read naturally and lose strobing.

match.note: Speed lines exist (fx); sub-frame motion blur on fast shots is WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Posterize-time style stepping so animation plays on twos or threes.
capabilities.pro_use: A hand-made, limited-animation look in motion graphics.

match.note: Stepped timing per shot or character, with identical frames deduplicated at render.

capabilities.capability: Data-driven animation: charts and properties driven from JSON or CSV files.
capabilities.pro_use: Infographics update by swapping the data file instead of re-animating.

match.note: film.data fetches cached sources, runs analysis scripts and binds results into text ({{path|format}}) and charts; it reports which shots and lines the new data changes.

capabilities.capability: Converting audio amplitude to keyframes to drive animation from sound.
capabilities.pro_use: Visuals that pulse to the music or the voice.

match.note: acting.plan places gestures from loudness, pitch and stress of the voice; film.beats gives the beat grid for cutting and cues. Raw amplitude-to-property mapping is not exposed.

capabilities.capability: Point tracking (one, two or four points, corner pin) and applying the track to another layer or effect.
capabilities.pro_use: Labels, screens and effects are stuck to moving objects in footage.

match.note: Doodleberry needs no image tracking: every element's position is known, so attaching to a moving part is exact. Tracking live footage is outside its scope.

capabilities.capability: Stabilising shaky footage (point stabilise and Warp Stabilizer).
capabilities.pro_use: Handheld plates are smoothed before compositing.

match.note: No live-action plates. The related need, compensating camera motion in Act it out takes, is in WP-12.

capabilities.capability: 3D Camera Tracker: solving camera motion from footage and placing 3D elements in the scene.
capabilities.pro_use: Integrating graphics and text into live-action shots with matched perspective.

match.note: Films are fully synthetic, so the camera is known exactly; there is nothing to solve.

capabilities.capability: Planar tracking through the bundled Mocha plug-in.
capabilities.pro_use: Screen replacements and tracking flat surfaces that rotate in perspective.

match.note: No footage pipeline.

capabilities.capability: Face tracking: following face outlines and detailed features (eyes, brows, mouth) to drive effects or animation.
capabilities.pro_use: Retouching, masking faces, or driving a character from a performer's face.

match.note: actout.clip reads face blendshapes (MediaPipe Face Landmarker) and makes eye, brow, gaze and mouth keys on a character; live tracking is WP-12.

capabilities.capability: Mask tracking: masks that follow an object through footage.
capabilities.pro_use: Isolating a moving region for colour or blur.

match.note: No footage to mask; masks themselves are a gap under Drawing and paths (WP-36).

capabilities.capability: Keying: Keylight and other colour keys with spill suppression and matte choking.
capabilities.pro_use: Pulling green-screen subjects and compositing them over new backgrounds.

match.note: No green-screen footage; Act it out reads pose from ordinary takes and never composites the performer. If live action is ever composited it would come with footage layers in WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Point and paragraph text layers with full typographic control: font, size, tracking, leading, alignment, fill and stroke.
capabilities.pro_use: Titles, lower thirds and on-screen copy set to a brand's type system.

match.note: Text comes as overlays (text, sign), kit elements (title, card, paper, quote, citation, wordmark), bubbles and styled captions (caption_style), in pinned OFL fonts with Sinhala fallback; per-character typographic control and narration boxes are WP-17.

capabilities.capability: Text animators with range, wiggly and expression selectors that animate properties per character, word or line.
capabilities.pro_use: Kinetic typography: words pop, cascade and jitter in designed patterns.

match.note: Word-highlight captions (burned in by film.render), per-word title pop-ins and voice-synced bubble reveals exist; general per-character animators are WP-15 (kinetic typography).

capabilities.capability: Text animation presets such as typewriter, fade or blur in by character or word.
capabilities.pro_use: Fast, consistent text reveals across a series.

match.note: Bubbles reveal word by word in sync with the voice; letter-by-letter typewriter with punctuation pauses is WP-17.

capabilities.capability: Text on a path, with characters flowing along a curve.
capabilities.pro_use: Titles that follow a shape, circular badges, text riding a line.

match.note: Not available; fits kinetic typography in WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Source-text expressions and data-driven text that change with other properties or a data file.
capabilities.pro_use: Counters, live numbers and template text filled from data.

match.note: Any text in shots.json or script lines can hold {{path|format}} bindings to data.json, and counter elements animate numbers.

capabilities.capability: Animating variable font axes such as weight and width (added in 26.0).
capabilities.pro_use: Type that breathes or swells for emphasis from one font file.

match.note: Not available; would be part of kinetic typography (WP-15).

capabilities.capability: Extruded 3D text and shapes with bevels in the Advanced 3D renderer.
capabilities.pro_use: Dimensional titles and logo stings.

match.note: No 3D text; the 3D layer (WP-42) would carry it.

capabilities.capability: Motion Graphics templates: packaging a composition with chosen editable controls for editors in another app.
capabilities.pro_use: Design teams ship branded lower thirds and titles that editors fill in without opening the project.

match.note: Format templates and kit elements take fields, and brand kits flow into every film that opts in; packaging rigs, boil presets and loop packs as reusable templates for others is WP-29.

capabilities.capability: Essential Properties: overriding chosen properties on each instance of a nested composition.
capabilities.pro_use: One master graphic used many times with different text, colour or image per instance.

match.note: Each use of a set or puppet can recolour or reconfigure it without copying the source; arbitrary property overrides would need nested scenes (WP-36).

capabilities.capability: Pasting text formatting and character styles between text layers (25.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Keeping type consistent across many titles.

match.note: Style is set centrally in the brand kit and caption style, so consistency is by construction rather than copy and paste.

capabilities.capability: Shape layers: parametric rectangles, ellipses, polygons and stars plus free Bezier paths with fills and strokes.
capabilities.pro_use: Flat-design motion graphics, icons and diagrams drawn inside the app.

match.note: Graphics are kit elements, code-drawn sets and Rig Canvas drawings for puppets; there are no parametric primitive shapes to place freely in a shot.

capabilities.capability: Shape operators: repeater, merge paths, offset paths, pucker and bloat, twist, round corners, zig zag.
capabilities.pro_use: Procedural patterns, bursts and stylised outlines from one simple shape.

match.note: No path operators; repeaters and instancing fit procedural 2D in WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Trim Paths: animating how much of a stroke is drawn, for write-on and line-draw reveals.
capabilities.pro_use: Signature reveals, routes on maps and diagrams that draw themselves.

match.note: The kit's draw element makes paths draw themselves and then optionally fill, timed to a line.

capabilities.capability: Wiggle paths and turbulent displacement for a hand-drawn, shimmering line.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives clean vector art a boiling, hand-made feel.

match.note: Deterministic line boil on characters, bubbles and signs (cycled seeds).

capabilities.capability: Tapered and wavy strokes on shape paths.
capabilities.pro_use: Expressive, ink-like lines from vector paths.

match.note: Pressure ink in the Rig Canvas, tapered strokes in the scene library and tapered speed lines; there is no per-stroke taper control in shots.json.

capabilities.capability: Masks: Bezier masks with feather (including variable feather), expansion, opacity and add/subtract/intersect modes.
capabilities.pro_use: Revealing parts of layers, vignettes, wipes and isolating regions for effects.

match.note: SVG clipping is used internally (toon shading, mesh triangles) and polygons cut parts on import, but there are no user masks in shots; masks and mattes are WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Paint tools: Brush, Clone Stamp and Eraser strokes on layers, frame by frame or held.
capabilities.pro_use: Hand-drawn effects, clean-up and quick touch-ups directly on footage.

match.note: No frame-by-frame painting; drawn levels and hand-drawn effects are WP-35, brush engines in WP-34.

capabilities.capability: Roto Brush and Object Matte: AI-assisted separation of a subject from its background across frames, with edge refinement.
capabilities.pro_use: Isolating people or objects in footage without hand rotoscoping.

match.note: No footage roto. The related need, click-to-mask cutting of drawings into parts (SAM 2.1), is WP-18; doodle.snap already suggests cuts automatically.

capabilities.capability: Content-Aware Fill: removing objects from footage by filling from surrounding frames.
capabilities.pro_use: Erasing rigs, signs or crew from live-action shots.

match.note: Every element is data, so unwanted things are deleted from the film rather than painted out.

capabilities.capability: Auto-trace: creating masks or paths from a layer's alpha or luminance.
capabilities.pro_use: Turning scanned artwork or logos into editable vectors.

match.note: puppet.from_ink thresholds ink to alpha and keeps the raster line; vector tracing (VTracer, potrace) is WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Alpha channels throughout: rendering, compositing and outputting with transparency.
capabilities.pro_use: Elements are rendered separately and layered, or delivered with alpha for other tools.

match.note: Synfig and Grease Pencil characters render with alpha and are composited over the set; delivering video with alpha (ProRes 4444, WebM) is WP-23.

capabilities.capability: Track mattes (alpha and luma, inverted) using any layer as the matte.
capabilities.pro_use: Text filled with footage, reveals through shapes, holdouts.

match.note: Not available; mattes are part of the node compositor (WP-36).

capabilities.capability: Adjustment layers that apply effects to everything below them for a time range.
capabilities.pro_use: One grade or blur across a group of layers, timed to a section.

match.note: The post finishing pass (grade, LUT, vignette, grain) applies to the whole joined picture before captions; per-shot or per-layer-range adjustment is WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Preserve underlying transparency, stencil and silhouette modes.
capabilities.pro_use: Textures confined to the art beneath, cut-outs through a stack.

match.note: Not available; belongs to the compositor (WP-36).

capabilities.capability: Compositing order and per-element depth switching.
capabilities.pro_use: Arms passing in front of and behind a body, props behind or in front of characters.

match.note: Elements stack in fixed bands, and puppets switch part order by control or clip (static in Lottie and Synfig, WP-14).

capabilities.capability: Glows, light wraps and edge blends to integrate elements from different sources.
capabilities.pro_use: Making graphics and characters sit naturally in a background.

match.note: Not available; WP-36 lists glows and light wraps.

capabilities.capability: Project bit depth of 8, 16 or 32-bit float, with linear-light blending.
capabilities.pro_use: High-end compositing avoids banding and blends light realistically.

match.note: 8-bit sRGB pipeline (Chromium capture to H.264); higher bit depth and EXR are WP-37.

capabilities.capability: ICC colour management: a working space, per-footage input profiles and output simulation.
capabilities.pro_use: Colour stays consistent across cameras, design files and deliverables.

match.note: Everything is assumed sRGB (Grease Pencil colours are converted to linear internally); colour management is WP-37.

capabilities.capability: OpenColorIO and ACES colour management with display and view transforms plus OCIO effects.
capabilities.pro_use: Film and VFX pipelines share one colour space across every app.

match.note: Planned in WP-37 (OpenColorIO, ACES).

capabilities.capability: Colour correction effects: curves, levels, hue and saturation, colour balance, Lumetri, and LUT application.
capabilities.pro_use: Grading shots to a look and matching elements to each other.

ref: shots.json post {preset, grade, lut, vignette, grain}
match.note: Film-wide finishing with presets (crisp, film, warm, cool, paper, noir), arbitrary ffmpeg grade filters and a .cube LUT. Per-shot grades and a colour script are WP-37.

capabilities.capability: HDR monitoring of compositions in HLG or PQ on local and external displays (25.2) and HDR metadata on export (25.4).
capabilities.pro_use: HDR deliverables are judged on a real HDR display while working.

match.note: SDR only; an HDR master is in WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Colour scopes (waveform, vectorscope, histogram) for judging exposure and colour.
capabilities.pro_use: Graders check legal levels and balance objectively.

match.note: brand.check measures palette contrast and colour-blind separation; checks on rendered frames (colour-blind, flash) are WP-24. No scopes.

capabilities.capability: Recolouring art consistently across a project.
capabilities.pro_use: Night versions, seasonal variants or a client's new brand colours.

match.note: Puppets use palette slots (puppet.lint flags raw colours) and sets recolour with set_opts; palette variants per scene (night, sick, cold) are WP-16.

capabilities.capability: A large built-in effect library, stacked per layer in any order with every parameter keyframable.
capabilities.pro_use: Most looks in motion graphics are built by stacking a few standard effects.

match.note: A fixed set of looks (toon shading, boil, motion fx, post grade/grain/vignette/LUT, depth-of-field blur in scene.js) with no general effect stack; the node compositor is WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Blur and sharpen effects: Gaussian, directional, camera lens blur, sharpen.
capabilities.pro_use: Depth cues, focus pulls and softening backgrounds.

match.note: Depth-of-field blur filters exist only in hand-coded scene.js films (engine/draw.js); a shot-level blur node is WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Distort effects: turbulent displace, warp, bulge, mesh warp, bend.
capabilities.pro_use: Organic wobble, hand-made shimmer and cartoon squish.

match.note: Turbulent displacement is the boil; squash and bendy limbs come from the rig. General warp effects are not available.

capabilities.capability: Generate effects: gradients, fractal noise, grids, fills, audio waveforms, strokes along paths.
capabilities.pro_use: Backgrounds, textures and design elements made without imported art.

match.note: Sets and kit elements are drawn in code as functions of time (paper, water, sections, roots and others); there is no general generator library.

capabilities.capability: Stylize effects: glow, cartoon, posterize, find edges, roughen edges.
capabilities.pro_use: Stylised and graphic looks from plain art.

match.note: style.toon gives cel shadows and rims; glow and stylize nodes are WP-36, and medium simulation for lines (pencil, marker, crayon) is WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Noise and grain effects: add, match and remove grain.
capabilities.pro_use: Film texture and matching grain between elements.

match.note: Seeded grain over the joined picture; matching and removal are not needed for synthetic frames.

capabilities.capability: Simulation effects: particle systems, shatter, card dance, foam, rain and snow.
capabilities.pro_use: Sparks, dust, weather and explosions in motion graphics.

match.note: Motion-derived dust puffs, impact stars and prop physics exist (fx, drop/flight); particle systems (rain, sparks, snow) are WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Time effects: echo, posterize time, time displacement, timewarp.
capabilities.pro_use: Trails, stepped motion and time-based distortions.

match.note: Stepped timing (style.step), speed lines, motion arcs and prop smears with multiples exist; echo, time displacement and timewarp are WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Transition effects: dissolves, linear, radial, gradient and block wipes, card wipes.
capabilities.pro_use: Moving between scenes and revealing graphics.

match.note: Cuts carry a whoosh and QA checks seam smoothness, but picture transitions (dissolves, match cuts, wipes) are WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Perspective effects: drop shadow, bevel alpha, 3D glasses, sphere wrap.
capabilities.pro_use: Depth on flat graphics and quick dimensional looks.

match.note: Characters get ground shadows (style.shadow); drop shadows on graphics are deliberately discouraged by the AI-look lint, other perspective effects would be WP-36 nodes.

capabilities.capability: Audio effects: EQ, reverb, delay, tone, and (26.0) gate and compressor, with level keyframes.
capabilities.pro_use: Basic sound shaping and level rides without leaving the comp.

match.note: film.render mixes automatically: voice cleanup and compression, ducking of music and effects, seeded room reverb, loudness to -14 LUFS with true-peak limiting, cue gains. Hand editing cues in a waveform lane is WP-40, room reverb per set WP-13.

capabilities.capability: Animation presets: saving effects, keyframes and expressions as a reusable preset and browsing a preset library.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios build libraries of reveals, bounces and looks to apply in one step.

match.note: Clips, poses, finishing presets and gag patterns are reusable presets that apply to any character on a template.

capabilities.capability: Effect Manager: seeing which effects and plug-ins are installed and turning them on or off.
capabilities.pro_use: Pipeline teams keep render nodes consistent and troubleshoot plug-in conflicts.

match.note: engine.info lists renderers and tools found; vendor.check lists vendored components. There is no effect plug-in interface to manage yet (open-source integration, WP-34).

capabilities.capability: Detail-preserving upscaling of footage.
capabilities.pro_use: Using low-resolution sources in high-resolution deliverables.

match.note: Vector art re-renders at any resolution; raster parts would need upscaling but none is planned.

capabilities.capability: JavaScript expressions on any property that compute its value every frame.
capabilities.pro_use: Procedural motion, rigs and automation without hand-placed keys.

match.note: Code films are expressions all the way down: every value is a pure function of the frame number. Shot-based films expose no per-property code; adding it would join WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Pick-whip linking: driving one property from another layer's property.
capabilities.pro_use: Rigging controls, linking a shadow to its object, chaining motion.

match.note: Driven keys map a control to angles, shifts, swaps and z; look-at and attachment link elements. No general property-to-property links in shots.

capabilities.capability: Expression controls (slider, checkbox, colour, point, angle, layer, dropdown) used as rig controls.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators drive a rig from a few named controls instead of many properties.

match.note: Named controls such as turn drive head three-quarter offsets and swaps; emotion, view and gaze are keyable controls on the acting timeline.

capabilities.capability: Looping and noise functions (loopOut, loopIn, wiggle, time-based maths).
capabilities.pro_use: Cycles, idles and organic jitter set once and left running.

match.note: Looping clips (idle, walk), travelling chain waves and seeded noise give the same results deterministically.

capabilities.capability: An expression editor with syntax checking and clear error messages.
capabilities.pro_use: Catching broken expressions before they reach a render.

match.note: Film data is checked against JSON schemas and its own references on every write and before every render, with errors reported; there is no code editor for scene.js.

capabilities.capability: Reading JSON and CSV data inside expressions to drive properties.
capabilities.pro_use: Data-driven graphics and template automation.

match.note: film.data runs analysis scripts into data.json and binds it into text and charts; it re-voices lines whose numbers change.

capabilities.capability: Scripting (ExtendScript and JavaScript) and script panels to automate project tasks.
capabilities.pro_use: Pipeline tools batch-create comps, rename layers, build renders and integrate with asset systems.

match.note: Every feature is a command reachable from CLI, HTTP, Studio and MCP; engine.commands lists them with schemas. This is Doodleberry's core strength.

capabilities.capability: Responsive design for time: protecting regions of a composition so stretching it keeps intros and outros intact.
capabilities.pro_use: Templates that change length without breaking their animation.

match.note: Times reference spoken lines, so film.retime re-derives shots after a voice change; script.slots fixes line slots before voicing.

capabilities.capability: The Advanced 3D renderer: a GPU renderer for 3D layers and models with realistic shading.
capabilities.pro_use: Motion designers add 3D objects to 2D designs without a separate 3D app.

match.note: A three.js renderer exists for hand-coded 3D pages (tools/three/run3d.mjs, software WebGL, about 1 s per frame) but not as a shot renderer or command; 3D sets and EEVEE passes are WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Playing embedded animations in imported 3D models and retiming them.
capabilities.pro_use: Animated product shots and characters from 3D apps used directly.

match.note: The three.js pages play GLB clips deterministically and CMU mocap can be retargeted in Blender (tools/blender), outside the command set; WP-42 brings it in.

capabilities.capability: Image-based lighting from HDR images, including animated environment lights (25.2).
capabilities.pro_use: Realistic reflections and ambient light that match a background.

match.note: Not available.

capabilities.capability: Cast and accept shadows per layer, and shadow catchers for grounding 3D objects on footage.
capabilities.pro_use: Making 3D objects sit in a scene.

match.note: 2D ground shadows and toon cel shadows only; 3D shadows come with WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Materials on 3D models and layers, including Substance 3D materials (26.0).
capabilities.pro_use: Changing the look of models without re-exporting them.

match.note: Not available.

capabilities.capability: Native parametric 3D meshes (cubes, spheres, cones; 26.0) created and animated inside a composition.
capabilities.pro_use: Simple 3D design elements without modelling software.

match.note: Not available.

capabilities.capability: 3D navigation and transform gizmos, a 3D design space, and extracting cameras and lights from models.
capabilities.pro_use: Fast staging of 3D scenes.

match.note: No 3D staging; scenes are 2D with a 2D camera.

capabilities.capability: In-renderer depth of field and depth data extraction.
capabilities.pro_use: Focus pulls and depth-based compositing.

match.note: Blur-based depth of field exists in scene.js films only; multiplane depth of field is WP-36, depth estimates for drawings in WP-43.

capabilities.capability: VR 360 and 180 tools: VR environments, a VR comp editor, immersive effects, cube-map output.
capabilities.pro_use: Producing 360-degree video for headsets and platforms.

match.note: Doodleberry targets flat social and web video; no 360 delivery is planned.

capabilities.capability: Stereoscopic 3D camera rigs.
capabilities.pro_use: Stereo deliverables for 3D cinema or headsets.

match.note: No stereo deliverables in scope.

capabilities.capability: Real-time cached playback using RAM and disk (a new high-performance preview engine in 25.2).
capabilities.pro_use: Animators judge timing at full speed while they work.

match.note: film.preview writes a live player page where every frame is a pure function of time, so it plays and scrubs without a render; export.web packages it as a standalone player.

capabilities.capability: Scrubbing, frame stepping and previewing from the current time in a range.
capabilities.pro_use: Checking a pose or a sync point frame by frame.

match.note: Studio /timeline scrubs the live player with clip, emotion, gaze and dialogue lanes from timeline.get.

capabilities.capability: Draft preview: lower resolution, skipped frames, region of interest, fast-draft modes.
capabilities.pro_use: Rough timing passes on heavy comps.

match.note: Different mechanism, same purpose: film.animatic holds storyboard stills over the sound in seconds; film.storyboard makes the stills and contact PDF.

capabilities.capability: Guides, grids, rulers and title/action-safe overlays in the viewer.
capabilities.pro_use: Keeping text and key action inside safe areas for each platform.

match.note: qa.run measures every word's box against the platform-safe area and minimum type sizes, with platform UI overlays; brand.assets also writes safe-area overlays.

capabilities.capability: Transparency grid and channel views (alpha, individual RGB channels; custom grid colours in 25.2).
capabilities.pro_use: Checking mattes and edges before delivering with alpha.

match.note: No alpha deliverables yet, so no alpha views; they come with alpha outputs in WP-23.

capabilities.capability: Video preview on an external broadcast monitor (Mercury Transmit), including HDR.
capabilities.pro_use: Colour-critical review on a calibrated display.

match.note: Not available; colour-critical and HDR review fit WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Snapshots and side-by-side views to compare two states of a frame.
capabilities.pro_use: Before-and-after checks of a tweak.

match.note: shot.render with a renderer override writes a second file for side-by-side comparison; a visual diff between two versions of a film is WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Render Queue with render settings and several output modules per item.
capabilities.pro_use: One render pass writes the master, a review proxy and an alpha version at once.

match.note: film.render writes the master (plus aspects, sound-off cut, captions); film.cuts assembles many cuts from it. Extra formats per render (WebM, ProRes, GIF, APNG) are WP-23.

capabilities.capability: Saved output-module and render-setting templates.
capabilities.pro_use: House delivery specs applied consistently.

match.note: Encoding profiles per platform (H.264 High CRF 18, AAC 48 kHz, faststart, size caps).

capabilities.capability: Codecs with alpha and intermediates (ProRes 4444, PNG sequences), and hand-off to Media Encoder for H.264 or HEVC.
capabilities.pro_use: Handing elements to editors and compositors at full quality.

match.note: H.264 masters only; alpha video and intermediates are WP-23.

capabilities.capability: Rendering still frames and image sequences (PNG, TIFF, EXR) including multi-channel output.
capabilities.pro_use: Posters, thumbnails, print stills and passes for further compositing.

match.note: Stills come from storyboards, covers and model sheets; print-ready stills are WP-23 and OpenEXR multi-pass output WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Multi-frame rendering that uses many CPU cores at once.
capabilities.pro_use: Large speed-ups on long or heavy renders.

match.note: Rendering runs a browser per worker on frame ranges and dedupes identical frames.

capabilities.capability: Command-line rendering (aerender) for unattended and scripted renders.
capabilities.pro_use: Render farms and overnight batches.

match.note: Every render is a command (CLI, HTTP with async jobs, MCP).

capabilities.capability: Network rendering and watch-folder rendering across several machines.
capabilities.pro_use: Splitting big jobs across a farm.

match.note: Single machine; distributed render workers and a shared cache are WP-38.

capabilities.capability: Exporting a composition as a Premiere Pro project for editing.
capabilities.pro_use: Moving finished graphics into the edit with structure intact.

match.note: film.cuts writes OTIO per cut; FCPXML and EDL with stems and captions are WP-22.

capabilities.capability: Notifications when a render finishes (desktop or mobile).
capabilities.pro_use: Artists leave long renders running and get pinged.

match.note: Async jobs exist but no progress events or webhooks; WP-20 (and owner notifications in WP-03).

capabilities.capability: Rendering audio along with picture and as separate stems.
capabilities.pro_use: Sound teams get clean stems for final mixing.

match.note: The mix writes stems and a music-only version; film.cuts reuses the master's stems.

capabilities.capability: Dynamic Link: compositions used live in Premiere Pro or Media Encoder without rendering first.
capabilities.pro_use: Editors see graphics updates in the edit immediately.

match.note: No live link; hand-off is by rendered cuts and OTIO. Round trips with editors are WP-22.

capabilities.capability: Round-trip editing of Photoshop and Illustrator sources, updating in the comp.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists repaint a layer and the animation updates.

match.note: puppet.export_layers hands a puppet to an artist as a layered file; puppet.import brings the repaint back onto the rig.

capabilities.capability: Cinema 4D integration through Cineware and the bundled C4D renderer.
capabilities.pro_use: 3D elements built in a companion app rendered inside the comp.

match.note: Doodleberry pairs with Blender (cut-out rigs in, Grease Pencil renderer out) and Synfig (.sif export); Blender 3D sets in films are WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Lottie export through the Bodymovin or LottieFiles plug-ins (third-party), for web and app animation.
capabilities.pro_use: UI and web animations made in After Effects play natively in apps.

match.note: export.lottie bakes one shot's puppet animation (views, swaps, lip-sync, springs) to Lottie JSON. dotLottie, Telegram stickers and Lottie QA in two renderers are WP-23.

capabilities.capability: Creative Cloud Libraries: shared colours, character styles and graphics across projects and team members.
capabilities.pro_use: Brand assets stay consistent across a team.

match.note: Brand kits, the cast library and the set library are shared, versioned data that every film can inherit.

capabilities.capability: A large third-party plug-in ecosystem (effects, rigging and particle tools).
capabilities.pro_use: Studios extend the app with specialised tools for particles, rigging and 3D.

match.note: Doodleberry vendors open-source code with recorded licences (vendor.check, vendor.build); a plan for driving or linking open tools (Natron, OpenFX, Krita brushes) is WP-34.

capabilities.capability: Round trip to an audio editor (Audition) for deeper sound work.
capabilities.pro_use: Cleaning dialogue and building sound design outside the comp.

match.note: Sound is mixed automatically; driving Audacity or Ardour and editing cues in Studio is WP-40.

capabilities.capability: Frame.io review: upload renders from the app and see reviewers' frame-accurate comments as timeline markers.
capabilities.pro_use: Client and director feedback arrives on the exact frame without email.

match.note: Notes are pinned to frames and review.fix turns them into data edits, re-renders and measures the change; review on a phone is WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Team Projects: a shared cloud project that several artists edit, publish and sync.
capabilities.pro_use: Editors and motion designers work on the same project at once.

match.note: Each film gets a git worktree and branch (prod.launch) and approved work merges in scope (prod.merge); people, roles and locks are WP-39.

capabilities.capability: Approval and version tracking for deliverables.
capabilities.pro_use: Knowing which version the client signed off.

match.note: The owner approves finals that passed QA; ledger.add records gate verdicts with before/after numbers; each post needs a named approval.

capabilities.capability: Syncing settings and presets between machines.
capabilities.pro_use: An artist's setup follows them to a new workstation.

match.note: The setup is in the repo: engine.doctor checks a machine and tools/setup.sh applies the fixes.

capabilities.capability: Collect Files: packaging a project with all its footage for hand-off or archive.
capabilities.pro_use: Archiving a job or sending it to another studio.

match.note: A film is text plus references to versioned cast, sets and manifest-tracked assets; renders are rebuilt rather than archived. There is no single zip export.

capabilities.capability: Persistent disk cache and RAM cache that keep rendered frames between sessions.
capabilities.pro_use: Reopening a project does not mean re-rendering everything.

match.note: Per-shot content hashes skip unchanged shots across sessions and identical frames are reused; build/ holds outputs.

capabilities.capability: GPU acceleration for rendering and effects.
capabilities.pro_use: Real-time playback of heavy effects.

match.note: The container has no GPU (software WebGL and Vulkan); GPU-only work waits for a GPU, per WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Proxies and low-resolution stand-ins for heavy footage.
capabilities.pro_use: Keeping interaction fast on big projects.

match.note: The animatic and storyboard stand in for the full render; a static-layer cache and rendering only unique stepped frames are WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Handling long, memory-heavy projects (purging, low-memory modes).
capabilities.pro_use: Feature-length or heavy VFX projects stay workable.

match.note: A long-form (20-minute) test of memory, cache and assembly limits is WP-38.

capabilities.capability: Diagnostics for GPU drivers and hardware readiness.
capabilities.pro_use: Ruling out the machine when something renders wrong.

match.note: engine.doctor reports every missing package, binary, model or voice with the exact fix.
